title: BA1/455/2023 of DR. DURGESH KUMAR Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT
NAINITAL
First Bail Application No. 455 of 2023
Dr. Durgesh Kumar S/o Tilakdhari Yadav .......Applicant

Present:- Mr. Ranbir Singh Kunda, Senior Advocate assisted by Mr.
M.L. Yadav and Mr. Tajhar Qayyum, Advocates for the
applicant.
Mr. Siddhartha Bisht, learned Brief Holders for the State.
Dated : 17.05.2023
Hon'ble Vivek Bharti Sharma, J. (Oral)
 Applicant Dr. Durgesh Kumar, who is in judicial
custody in Case Crime/F.I.R. No. 235 of 2022, under Sections
376, 376(2)(e), 376(2)(f), 354 & 506 of I.P.C., Police Station
Pantnagar, District Udham Singh Nagar has sought his
release on bail.
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused
the record available on file.
3. Learned senior counsel for the applicant/accused
would submit that the applicant is a Government employee,
and a Medical Doctor posted at Govind Ballabh Pant
Agriculture & Technical University, Pantnagar, District
Udham Singh Nagar; he has unblemished career and no
previous similar allegation against him; he is an innocent
person; he has been falsely implicated in the present case; the
chargesheet has already been filed in the present case,

2
therefore, there is no possibility of tampering with the
evidence by the applicant/accused. He would further submit
that the alleged incident is of 05.12.2022 and there is six
days delay in registration of the F.I.R. i.e. on 11.12.2022;
there is no explanation in the chargesheet for the said delay.
He would further submit that on the date of the alleged
incident the applicant/accused was checking the patients in
the O.P.D. of the Hospital of the University and there were
135 patients on the alleged date of incident of molestation
and sexual assault by the applicant/accused upon the
victim/complainant; as per the case of the prosecution she
was outdoor patient at Sl.No. 80. He drew the attention of the
Court of the statement of one Beena Arya (annexed at page
no.112 attached with the counter affidavit), wherein she stated
that she was working in the Hospital of the University at the
post of Sweeper since last 15 years and apart from this duty
she was also assigned the duty of sending the patients to the
applicant Dr. Durgesh Kumar for medical check up one by
one; on 05.12.2022, the alleged date of incident, she was also
present in the Hospital and was assigned the duty of sending
the patient to the applicant/accused for medical check up as
other two Doctors, namely, Dr. Deepak Tripathi and Dr. Ritu
Tripathi were on leave; that, she does not know that if at all
the applicant/accused did any wrong act with the
victim/complainant, nor she told anything to me when she
came out from inside after her medical examination by the

3
applicant/accused; that, she did not know that if the
applicant/accused had done any of such act with any other
girl. He would further submit that Beena Arya is the only
independent witness of the case, who was present at the
alleged place of occurrence at the time of alleged incident of
sexual assault by the applicant upon the victim/complainant.
Learned counsel for the applicant would further submit that
there is a specific averment of the complainant in her F.I.R.
that applicant/accused told that the complainant was
suffering from urinary infection, but, notwithstanding this
averment no medical examination for urinary infection of the
victim/complainant was done that, had this medical
examination for urinary infection been done then it would
have been a strong piece of evidence; that, no purpose would
be served by keeping the applicant behind the bars as the
trial is likely to take long time.
4. Mr. Siddhartha Bisht, Brief Holder for the State. He
drew attention of this Court to the statement of one Mr.
Siddhanth, the classmate and friend of the
victim/complainant, recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C.
(annexed at page no.64 with the counter affidavit), where he
stated that when the victim/complainant came out from the
room of the applicant/accused after her medical examination
she was crying and told him that she was physically violated
by the applicant/accused with his finger into her vagina.

4
5. Learned senior counsel for the applicant/accused
contested the presence and truthfulness of this witness,
Siddhanth as there was no mention of his name in the F.I.R.
consequently statements of the said witness is not tenable.
6. Considering the facts and circumstances of the
case, but, without expressing any opinion on the final merits
of the case this Court is of the view that it is a case for bail.
7. Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.
8. Let the applicant Dr. Durgesh Kumar be released
on bail on furnishing bail bond with two sureties in the
amount of Rs. 80,000/- and personal bond in the like amount
to the satisfaction of the court concerned. In addition, it is
also directed as under:-
(i) The applicant will not leave the country.
(ii) The applicant shall also undertake that he will
not contact any of the witnesses of the charge-sheet
and any of their family members.
(iii) The applicant shall not try to tamper with the
evidence.
9. The Senior Superintendent of Police, Udham Singh
Nagar is directed to examine the matter about the lack of
professionalism shown by the Investigating Officer in not
getting the medical examination in respect of the facts of
infection stated in her F.I.R.. Had the medical examination of

5
the complainant for the alleged infection, as stated in the
F.I.R., been done then this would have been an important
piece of evidence for dispensation of justice. He is further
directed to place his report before the trial court.
 (Vivek Bharti Sharma, J.)
 17.05.2023
Mamta
